claims.statement: EU WEEE rules require item-level functionality testing, records, direct-reuse documentation, and protective transport evidence to treat shipped reclaimed electrical equipment as used equipment rather than presumptively illegal waste.
Poland's 1.6 million-plus microinstallations and a documented 10-15-year inverter service life create a real future repair and replacement base, especially for off-warranty electronics.
Module reuse economics are weak today: JRC reports low warranty returns, roughly 30-year module life, and refurbishment costs that can exceed new production costs.

SecondSol already operates the near-exact European marketplace with more than 60000 users, over 250000 spare parts, used and refurbished components, testing, repair, auctions, logistics, and recycling.
A viable Polish wedge must focus on documented fitment for obsolete, off-warranty components unavailable from OEM replacement channels, not generic used modules.

contrary_evidence: SecondSol already has the same marketplace, testing, repair, auction, logistics, and spare-part scope at European scale.
SMA sends current-portfolio replacement devices, reducing demand for reclaimed units where OEM substitution is technically feasible.
JRC finds module return rates low and present refurbishment economics inferior to cheap new modules.
Second-life PV repair methods and assurance standards remain incompletely standardized.

economics.acquisition_route: Seed obsolete part numbers and service histories from the family installer and two to five licensed recycler or repair partners; acquire technicians through exact part-number search and installer procurement workflows.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: An unvalidated path requires about 70 million PLN annual GMV at a 10% blended take rate and roughly 30% EBITDA margin; at a four-times EBITDA value and at least 70% founder ownership, equity could exceed 5 million PLN in seven to ten years.
economics.founder_time: About 15-20 hours weekly only if testing, warehousing, electrical work, and waste handling are performed by qualified partners.
economics.gross_margin_basis: An inventory-light marketplace can retain software margin, but testing, return, fraud, support, and fitment-guarantee costs make the original 45% gross margin unvalidated.
economics.payback: At an unvalidated 150 PLN contribution per completed order, 500 completed orders recover 75000 PLN before founder salary.
economics.pricing: Charge an 8-12% take rate plus 100-300 PLN for documented third-party testing; higher fees require demonstrated scarcity or avoided redesign labor.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Technicians may repeat across failures, but OEM replacements and SecondSol are substitutes and each part-number market is fragmented.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A Poland-specific graph linking serials, electrical compatibility, test evidence, installation context, and successful repairs
fingerprint.customer: Solar repair technicians, licensed recyclers, and owners of aging off-warranty PV systems
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Long-tail part-number search, installer procurement accounts, and recycler inventory feeds
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fitment-guaranteed managed exchange for tested obsolete PV components with take rate and test fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Repairer pays when a tested compatible component ships and the platform guarantees the documented fitment
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An off-warranty legacy inverter, optimizer, or module fails and OEM replacement is unavailable or requires costly redesign

founder_fit: The family installer can supply early failure cases and verify whether fitment pain is real.
Data modeling and marketplace automation match the founder's technical strengths.
Licensed partners must own electrical testing, waste handling, warehousing, and installation so the business remains part-time.
risks: Untested or poorly documented goods can be treated as WEEE, including illegal-shipment consequences.
A substantial modification can shift manufacturer-like product liability to the modifier; even ordinary resale carries conformity and defect exposure.
SecondSol's established liquidity and services make a broad European marketplace non-differentiated.
OEM current-product replacement can be safer and cheaper than reclaimed fitment.
Rare-part liquidity fragments by model, voltage, firmware, grid code, and vintage.

structure.control_point: Documented serial-level fitment, functionality test, and successful-repair record
structure.critical_dependency: Qualified non-waste supply, conservative testing and liability rules, and local liquidity not already captured by SecondSol or OEM replacements

thesis: Build a managed Polish exchange for tested, obsolete, off-warranty photovoltaic components, using item-level fitment and successful-repair evidence to guarantee compatibility where OEM replacement would otherwise require costly redesign.
title: PV Fitment Exchange
uncertainties: The annual count and avoided cost of Polish legacy-component failures are unknown.
SecondSol's Polish usage, seller fees, fulfillment performance, and inventory coverage are unknown.
Testing, return, insurance, warranty, and fitment-guarantee costs have not been quoted.
It is unknown which reclaimed component classes remain non-waste and safe after recycler intake.
No evidence yet proves technicians will switch procurement or contribute fitment outcomes.
